Subject: Expired sandbox — can we reopen for pilot?

Hi Karthik,

Quick context: we recently closed an acqui-hire (internal reorg) and our engineering team lost access to the Redwood sandbox we were using for a short pilot. The credits expired last week and our CI smoke tests now fail — we still have a small set of evals to run before we can finalize our vendor recommendation.

Can Redwood reactivate the sandbox or grant a short-term credit top-up so we can finish the evaluation? We are prepared to sign an MOU outlining limited use and short retention for this pilot. If you need an internal PO or legal statement, I can pull that together quickly.

Relevant details:
- Prior sandbox project name: forman-sandbox-2026
- Active test suite: embedding performance + latency regression (approx 50k tokens/week)
- Desired extension: 2 weeks or ~15k tokens, whichever you prefer

I can send the signed MOU by EOD tomorrow. Appreciate any one-time assistance to avoid re-running work from scratch.

— Jessica
Jessica Forman

Hi Jessica — thanks for the context and for the quick offer to sign an MOU. Welcome the heads-up about the acquisiton reorg (congrats).

We can do a one-time reactivation while legal signs off on an MOU. Two options we typically offer for situations like this:
1) Short bridge: 15k tokens + 14 days sandbox access (fast, manual approval)
2) Scoped reactivation: 30 days with a lightweight MOU and SOC 2 readout (requires legal review — ~24–48h)

To move immediately, please:
- Upload the MOU to the Drive link I just shared (or return signed PDF)
- Confirm whether you need isolated data handling / private deployment for this pilot (that will affect provisioning)

Aditya — can you approve a one-time 15k token bridge for Forman Labs if they provide a signed MOU? Monica — can you prepare an onboarding ticket so we can fast-track the sandbox once approvals land?

Jessica — if you want I can provision the temporary sandbox today and hold the bridge credit pending the signed MOU.

Thanks,
